text: dsh-readme 是一个 DSH 插件，会在每次模型步骤组装系统提示词时读取用户指定的文本文件，并将其作为工作约束段提供给主 agent 和子 agent。它通过 bundle patch 注册插件，并在 systemPrompt 服务中添加动态文本段；相对路径按会话工作目录解析，文件内容可按配置限制大小、缓存或在变化时重读。用户可从插件设置页指定文件和调整选项。适合希望让项目约定或团队规则在整个会话中持续生效的 DSH 用户。需要配置本地文本文件路径，不需要 API key 或外部服务。

dsh-readme adds a chosen text file to the DSH system prompt at each model step, including subagents. Relative paths use the session directory, and a settings page configures the file. It keeps project conventions available throughout a session; no API key or external service is required.
想让项目里的约定在 DSH 每次回答时都能参考
怎么把一份本地规则文件自动放进 agent 的系统提示词？
Keep a local instructions file in the prompt for every model step.
dsh-readme 的功能「持续注入工作约束」：在系统提示词组装时读取配置的文本文件，并将其作为约束段加入每个模型步骤，主 agent 和子 agent 都可获得。路径可相对会话工作目录设置；文件变化时可重新读取。
dsh-readme 的功能「在插件设置页配置文件」：插件在 DSH 的 Plugins 设置区域提供配置入口，用户可指定约束文件路径并保存到 profile；配置支持开关、最大注入字节数、文件变化时重读和缺失文件处理方式。

dsh-readme README · dsh-readme：**English** · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

Read one text file — a team conventions file, a project's `AgentsReadMe.md`, a
style guide — and inject its contents into the system prompt of **every** agent
before that agent's first model request. The file's rules then apply for the whole
session, in that session's main agent and in every subagent it spawns.

dsh-readme README · Why a system prompt section and not a message：DSH assembles the system prompt before each model step, from ordered sections. A
section's text may be a function, so it is re-evaluated per step. Mounting the file
as a section therefore needs no session hooks at all: there is no step that could
send a request without first assembling the section, so "read before the first run"
is a structural guarantee rather than a race the plugin tries to win.
section: Why a system prompt section and not a message

text:
dsh-readme README · Why a system prompt section and not a message：It also survives context compression. A file fed in as a chat message can be
summarised away half an hour later; a system-prompt section cannot.
section: Why a system prompt section and not a message

text:
dsh-readme README · Install：The plugin is a normal DSH bundle. Either install it from a directory:

```bash
dsh plugin add /path/to/dsh-readme
```

or point the profile at it by hand — add the package to `dependencies` and to
`dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `package.json`, then reinstall:

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-readme": "file:/path/to/dsh-readme" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-readme", "..."] } }
}

Restart DSH afterwards: bundle rows are read at startup.

dsh-readme README · If the plugin stops loading：A profile selects its plugins by name in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The plugin manager
rebuilds that list whenever it installs or removes **any** package, and it keeps an
existing entry only while `node_modules/<name>/package.json` still declares
`dsh.bundle.patch`. A package directory that is momentarily absent — an interrupted
install, a reinstall, a manual cleanup — therefore drops out of the list silently,
and it does not come back on its own. The plugin stays in `dependencies`, its
settings stay in the profile patch, and nothing loads it.

dsh-readme README · If the plugin stops loading：Two ways to see it. In the app, the constraint section is simply absent from the
prompt. From a shell:

```bash
node scripts/profile-check.mjs desktop
```

dsh-readme README · If the plugin stops loading：The script reads the profile (not a checkout of this repository), reports the
dependency, the bundle row, the installed copy, the patch and the configured file,
and exits non-zero when one of them is wrong. If the row is the missing piece, add
the name back to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `package.json` and restart.
The same condition shows up at startup as:

```
dsh: [.../cordis.patch.yml] patch: entry "dsh-readme" not found
```

dsh-readme README · Configure：The plugin ships its own configuration page, registered on the plugin page's
`plugins.row.config` seat: open **Settings → Plugins**, open the bundle that lists
this row, then use `Configure` on the `dsh-readme` row to edit the path and save.
The write goes to the active profile's patch document and needs no restart — the
next prompt assembly reads the new file.

dsh-readme README · Configure：The page reads and writes the form state the host hands it, so validation, revision
conflicts and the read-only fallback are the host's, not the plugin's: a write
carries a `revision` and a stale one is reported as a conflict; a field already
fixed by the profile patch or a command-line overlay shows as read-only instead of
being silently dropped.

Every field can also be written by hand in the profile patch:

```yaml

dsh-readme README · name is rejected as a "name mismatch" and the whole patch entry is skipped.：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Inject at all. Off means the plugin writes nothing into the prompt. |
| `path` | `""` | The file. Supports `~`, `$VAR`, `${VAR}`, `%VAR%`. A relative path resolves against the **session's** working directory. Empty means "not configured yet", and the plugin stays silent. |
| `maxBytes` | `32768` | Cap on injected text, 1024–4194304. A longer file is truncated **and the model is told so**, because a model that assumes it read the whole file will confidently violate the part that was cut. |
| `reloadOnChange` | `true` | Re-read when the file changes. Off pins the first read for the life of the mount, which keeps the prompt byte-identical across steps and friendlier to prompt caching. |
| `onMissing` | `notice` | What to inject when the file cannot be read: `notice` puts one line in the prompt telling the model to say so; `silent` injects nothing. |
| `order` | `520` | Position in the prompt. 520 is after the plan policy (500) and before the team policy (600). |

dsh-readme README · name is rejected as a "name mismatch" and the whole patch entry is skipped.：Each setting can also come from the environment (`DSH_README_ENABLED`,
`DSH_README_PATH`, `DSH_README_ORDER`, `DSH_README_MAX_BYTES`,
`DSH_README_RELOAD_ON_CHANGE`, `DSH_README_ON_MISSING`), which is useful for a
headless deployment with no panel. Precedence: configuration wins, the environment
is the deployment default, the built-in defaults are last. An empty string does not
override anything — it falls through to the layer beneath.

dsh-readme README · 工作约束（来自 dsh-readme）：用户为这个会话指定了一份约束文件，下面是它的全部内容，在本次会话处理第一个请求之前已经读取。
这些条目是**强制规范**：它们优先于通用默认做法、工具的使用建议和你自己的习惯。
若它们与任何其他说明冲突，以此处为准；如果某条要求在本任务里无法执行，先说明原因，再按最接近的方式做。
不要复述、摘要或转述这份文件——直接照着它工作。

来源：~/notes/conventions.md · 共 1240 字节 · 2026-10-24 21:40

---
（文件内容，原样）
---
```

dsh-readme README · 工作约束（来自 dsh-readme）：The framing is deliberate. "Here is a file" reads as reference material the model
may weigh against its defaults, which is exactly what a constraints file exists to
prevent; the header instead states where the authority comes from, what wins a
conflict, and — the line that keeps the injection affordable — that the file is not
to be echoed back.

dsh-readme README · Behaviour details：- **Read lazily, on the first assembly.** Not at plugin load. A session started
  hours after install sees the file as it is now.
- **Cached by `(path, size, mtime)`.** An unchanged file costs one `stat` per step,
  not a read.
- **Missing, empty, binary, directory, unreadable:** each has its own state. An
  empty file or an unconfigured path injects nothing at all — injecting an empty
  header would spend tokens on every step to say nothing.
- **Binary files are refused** (a NUL in the first 8 KiB), so pointing `path` at a
  zip by mistake produces a notice instead of mojibake in the prompt.
- **Truncation cuts on a UTF-8 boundary**, never mid-character, and a BOM is
  stripped.
- **`{{...}}` in the file is literal text**: the section is registered with
  `interpolate: false`, so a README documenting a template is not rewritten by the
  prompt renderer.
- **One section per mount**, named `dsh-readme:constraints`. Do not add a second
  row for this plugin to a preset; two instances would register the same section
  name twice.

dsh-readme README · Tests：```bash
node test/smoke.mjs
```

No DSH host, no network, no `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`: the test covers path
expansion, every read state, the binary and truncation guards, the cache and the
rendered text.
